findings.claim: Construct 3 in NW.js, not RPG Maker or Electron
13 nonzero plane definitions, plus separate otherworld/divine-world structures; table rows alone do not prove reachability
Each plane has local town services, factions, currency types, material yields and difficulty; currency types can be shared
Enter-plane handler records current plane in save[36,1,0], clears otherworld slot save[88,1,0], changes map and resets encounter selectors
Shared actor/item/career tables and selection handlers support a roster traveling between themed destinations; exhaustive retention and companion consent are unproved
Career changes make incompatible learned skill types ineffective; local service access, learning and current usability differ
Drop consumer uses named weighted drop/no-drop tables; common item branch clamps boosted weights against 10000, with a separate 100-scale material branch
Plane 3 has the endless tower, plane 4 beast hunting, plane 8 rebirth, plane 10 an abyss rift
Rebirth compares tier, level, destiny-slot and material requirements, then increments tier and level in the inspected successful branch
Antique shop sells plane equipment for home cash; company research and buildings support further growth and expeditions
Normal and backup saves serialize Construct arrays to LocalStorage or NW.js files using slot metadata; disk and LocalStorage routes are conditional
Base-time and auto-combat groups exist; battle speed is stated to leave city management time unchanged; closed-app catch-up remains unread
Dialogue executor joins text, speaker and portrait with typewriter rendering and special-event handling; full branch/condition semantics remain partial
Package declares a resizable 2016x1136 window and a 2560x1440 main layout; native 1366x768 legibility is untested
Plane progress reader clamps packed progress to 0..1001 and derives a 1..10 difficulty and within-band 1..100 floor
This source is strongest for acquisition and useful homeward loops; it does not establish simulated resident lives or persistent interpersonal cross-world history
